subject: AcmeHealth pricing targets & benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Liu <sam.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + ask: target $/1M tokens & volumes

Hi Sam — great to meet today. Quick recap and two asks so we can get you a tight proposal: 

1) Volume profile: please confirm expected production token volumes (avg monthly inference tokens and any known spikes). You mentioned POC ~50M/month moving to 1B/month in 12 months — is that still the model?

2) Target economics: procurement asked for a target price per 1M tokens that would make Redwood competitive. If you can share a range (e.g., $X–$Y per 1M tokens) that helps us propose committed tiers.

What I committed to: by EOD Thursday we’ll send a short benchmarking snapshot vs the major hosts (OpenAI, Anthropic, other open-hosts) and a plausible committed-discount schedule tied to the volumes you call out.

Attachment: - MAP-AcmeHealth.pdf (mutual action plan stub)

Next steps: reply with the production volume range and any internal target $/1M. If you prefer, I can draft two scenarios: conservative (no commit) and committed (12-month/committed throughput).

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Diego: +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Sam Liu <sam.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: AcmeHealth procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: target $/1M tokens & volumes

Thanks Diego — quick answers inline.

- Volume: POC (Q4): ~40–60M tokens/month. Production (H1 next year): 600–900M tokens/month with occasional peaks to ~1.2B for campaigns. We expect steady ramp starting Jan.

- Target economics: procurement is looking for target around $150–$250 per 1M tokens for committed usage, but they also asked for an uncommitted (pay-as-you-go) comparator.

Timeline: procurement wants a commercial term sheet and SOW draft by Oct 16 to hit our internal procurement cycle. Also need SOC2 in-scope info + any data retention guarantees.

Sam Liu
Head of AI Platform, AcmeHealth
sam.liu@acmehealth.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Liu <sam.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: target $/1M tokens & volumes

Sam — thank you for the clarity. Per our commitment, attached is a concise benchmarking snapshot and two commercial scenarios. See highlights below (high-level numbers, rounded):

Benchmark (representative $/1M tokens, public/market rates + inferred list pricing for typical Gen‑text workloads):
- OpenAI (gpt-4.1-style hosted): $650/1M (uncommitted); committed can approach $300–$400/1M at scale (enterprise deals).
- Anthropic (Claude-like): $420/1M (uncommitted); committed ~220–$320/1M depending on term.
- Other open-model hosts (VM/replicated-managed): $200–$350/1M (varies with q8/q4 quantization and KV cache patterns).

Redwood suggested targets for AcmeHealth (based on your 600–900M steady state):
- No-commit (hosted, pay-as-you-go): $290/1M (includes streaming + latency SLAs) — competitive vs the open-host average given the SLA and prefix caching we provide.
- Committed 12mo (commit to 600M/month): $160/1M — tiered discounts apply at 600M+, 900M+, 1.2B+; includes prefix/KV cache savings and batch optimizations.

Why Redwood comps well: our serving runtime reduces per-token CPU/GPU overheads (prefix caching and dynamic batching) so committed economics show larger gains vs pure managed hosts. We also included a conservative scenario assuming 20–30% effective quantization lift (practical for many of your transformer workloads).

Attachments: 
- pricing-comparison-$/1M.xlsx (benchmark sheet with per-host assumptions)
- redwood-pricing-summary.pdf (two commercial scenarios + caveats)
- MAP-AcmeHealth.pdf (mutual action plan, updated)

Next actions I propose:
1) I’ll draft a short commercial term sheet + SOW (to hit Oct 16).
2) Vanessa (cc’d) can cover SOC2 + data retention commitments; Vanessa, can we confirm scope we can deliver for AcmeHealth (KMS options, retention windows, audit logs)?

If $160/1M (committed) is inside your procurement target range, I’ll prioritize the formal quote with committed tiers. If procurement wants tighter (<$150/1M), we can look at longer term or higher commit floors.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Liu <sam.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: AcmeHealth procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: target $/1M tokens & volumes

Diego — this is helpful, thanks. Two quick confirmations: 

1) The procurement target band ($150–$250/1M) was a rough ask; $160/1M committed at 600M/mo fits our internal target window. Please proceed with a formal commercial term sheet and SOW by Oct 16.

2) Procurement will need SOC2 attestations and specifics on retention + encryption (we require KMS integration and 90-day default retention with options to extend). Vanessa, can you send the SOC2 artifact and an outline of retention/KMS options?

Procurement (procurement@acmehealth.com) — looping you in to sync on timeline and formatting for the term sheet.

Sam
